label: TMUA 2023 · Paper 2 · Question 14
knowledgePattern: Exploit a cyclic slope product when two parameterised lines are perpendicular
solution:
The slopes are m1=−a/b, m2=−b/c, m3=−c/a. Their product is −1, since a,b,c are nonzero.

If any two lines are perpendicular, the product of their slopes is−1. Dividing the three-slope product by that pair product gives slope 1 for the remaining line. It is parallel to y=x, so F is always true.

The other claims need not hold. With (a,b,c)=(1,2,4) the slopes are −1/2,−1/2,−4, disproving A–D. For E and G, take (1,2,−1): the lines are y=−x/2+1/2, y=2x+1, y=x−2. The first two are perpendicular, but the third is not parallel to y=−x, and their three lines do not meet at one point. Answer F.

hints.title: Write all three slopes
hints.body: Put each line into slope-intercept form. Look for a simple relation between the three gradient expressions.
hints.recap: For nonvertical lines, perpendicular slopes multiply to−1 and parallel lines have equal slopes.
hints.pitfall: Carry each minus sign through the cyclic ratios.
hints.pause: Calculate a symmetric product of the three slopes.

recall.reminder: For nonvertical lines, perpendicular slopes multiply to−1 and parallel lines have equal slopes.

hints.title: Use a pair condition in the relation
hints.body: Suppose a pair is perpendicular and substitute that information into the relation you found. Then check the listed conclusions for the remaining line.
hints.recap: A sufficient condition must guarantee its conclusion for every permitted case.
hints.pitfall: A gradient condition alone says nothing about a common intersection point.
